description:
Eliminate the remaining per-call cost of profile-driven selection at the five pinned bit-backend entry points, keeping the profile in charge of the boundary at every pinned size.

## Background

The second post-cutover receipt, `dev/benchmarks/tuning_profiles/2026-08-20-post-cutover-receipt-2.md`, records `RESULT: FAIL` at eleven of the thirty-four pinned cells and on the set statistic. At the two cells the first excursion named, the ratio rises further under `c42720ce`'s threshold cache: `bit_backend/popcount/words=1` from 1.182311 to 1.294670 and `bit_backend/popcount/words=8` from 1.064214 to 1.123171. Measured against the same-session control build, the bit-backend `words=1` cells pay 0.4–0.7 ns/call in the post-cutover binary. The measurement decides against the reduction: `c42720ce` left the fast path an `Acquire` flag load, a branch, and a `Relaxed` value load, and that path still pays a material fraction of the cheapest pinned operations.

Owner decision DEC-E (2026-08-20) scopes the rework of the second excursion as two tracks. This issue is track 1: eliminate the real per-call cost at the selection boundary. Sibling track 2 predeclares the attribution amendment to the verdict procedure; whether this issue's mechanism suffices at the pinned cells is decided there, under `50b47eae`, not here. τ_cell stays 5 % and τ_set stays 2 %.

Constraints carried forward from `dev/active/220cab0b/design.md` §4 and `c42720ce`:

- The profile keeps governing the boundary at every pinned size, including the calibrated `simd_min_words` = 4 below the conservative default of 8. A compiled-in floor is rejected in `c42720ce`'s Background: any floor high enough to fix `words=8` makes the calibration inert.
- Selection semantics are preserved exactly: the same comparison operator and sense, the same conservative default with no profile installed, the same code in a build without the `simd` feature.
- No build script, no environment reads in library code, no new crate dependency edges.
- `usize::MAX` stays an admissible threshold per design §2.1; no value is reserved as a sentinel.
- No in-source default moves, no pinned cell changes, the `selector-non-regression-v1` schema token is not bumped, `crates/gf2-core/src/field/poly.rs` is untouched.
- Committed tests of other issues are not edited: adding assertions to a default-profile binary is acceptable; changing existing assertions or `required-features` is not.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: On the resolved fast path, each pinned bit-backend entry point pays at most one `Relaxed` atomic load plus the existing comparison per call — no flag load and no resolution branch — and the mechanism is recorded as an additive amendment to design §4.1 that changes no pre-existing line.
- [hard] REQ-02: `select_backend_for_size` keeps its current selection semantics exactly: the same comparison operator and sense, the same conservative default when no profile is installed, and the same behaviour in a build without the `simd` feature.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test observes through the production route-observation API (from `697fc55b`) that an installed profile whose `simd_min_words` differs from the default, including a value below it, still moves the selected route. Equivalence assertions between routes prove nothing here and do not satisfy this.
- [hard] REQ-04: A committed artefact records the selection boundary's instruction sequence at the pinned entry points before and after the change and states the delta; the elimination is visible in the instructions, not inferred.
- [hard] REQ-05: If REQ-01 cannot hold together with REQ-02 and profile governance at every pinned size, the issue delivers the demonstration of that impossibility and stops for escalation instead of shipping a further reduction.

## Notes

Whether the elimination brings the pinned comparison inside the predeclared tolerance is decided by the amended verdict procedure under `50b47eae`. This issue delivers the mechanism and its instruction-level evidence; it runs no benchmark-mode session.
title: Eliminate the per-call cost of the bit-backend selection boundary
